data.name: Aydinun
data.gender_notes: Aydinun is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from 'Ayd', meaning 'lord' or 'master', and 'dunya', meaning 'world'. Aydinun is the one who brings light and guidance to the world. The name Aydinun carries the meaning “Light of the world” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aydinun usually hope their child will grow to embody light of the world and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aydinun is a spiritual name that reflects the belief in the divine gift of life and the blessings of God. It is a reminder of the importance of gratitude and living a life in accordance with the will of God.
data.etymology: Aydinun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light of the world.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aydinun total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aydinun holds a significant impact on Arab and Islamic culture as a symbol of leadership and guidance. In Islamic history, examples of leaders with this name include the 16th-century Turkish Sultan Aydogdu Mehmed and preacher Aydun Ali, a famous Khawaja from the Chishtia Sufi order. The name continues to be popular in the Middle East and the wider Islamic world and carries an air of authority and wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic belief, Aydinun is an affirmation of faith, a reminder that a believer is a servant of Allah (God). The name encapsulates the spiritual ideals of submission to the divine will and seeking light and guidance from Allah in the transient world. Aydinun is also associated with the concept of siddiq (truthful and righteous) and the Ahl al-Bayt (Prophet Muhammad's family), who are believed to be the embodiment of truth and guidance.
